lines.name: North Shore Line

segments.routing: Glover Wharf (Beverly Harbor) → Salem Sound → Salem Wharf (Blaney St). Short sheltered-sound hop; sea-state gate still applies to the sound entrance.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan — displacement speed on the entire downtown approach; foil-borne only Salem Sound → Broad Sound → President Roads
segments.routing: Salem Sound exit past Marblehead/Nahant → open Broad Sound (semi-open Atlantic; sea-state exposure) → President Roads → cross the no-wake boundary at Logan's NW corner → inner harbor main channel → Long Wharf. Keep clear of Logan runway-approach areas; do NOT place a Logan call (held corridor).

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Long Wharf → across the inner harbor/Fort Point Channel mouth → Fan Pier dock. Displacement speed throughout; do not enter Fort Point Channel interior.

lines.phase_notes: Navier's flagship edge — the MBTA does not serve Salem; the seasonal Salem Ferry already sells commuter-rate rush-hour tickets, proving a private operator monetizes this commute. Phase 1 runs Salem ↔ Long Wharf ↔ Fan Pier; the Beverly extension is Phase 2 (renders dimmed until then — Glover Wharf municipal marina is ready today). Marblehead extension is HELD on the watchlist pending a negotiated recurring berth — do not render Marblehead. Foil-borne across Broad Sound, displacement inside the harbor: target ~35–45 min Salem→Seaport is modeled, unverified — render only as indicative. Weather-cancellation policy applies; Salem and Beverly have commuter-rail fallback.

lines.name: South Shore Express

segments.routing: Hewitts Cove → Hingham Bay → Nantasket Roads → Pemberton Point pier.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan — displacement speed on the downtown approach; foil-borne only across Nantasket Roads / President Roads
segments.routing: Pemberton Point → Nantasket Roads → President Roads (foil-borne) → cross the no-wake boundary at Logan's NW corner → inner harbor main channel → Rowes Wharf.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Rowes Wharf → across the inner harbor → Fan Pier. Displacement speed throughout.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone (short Seaport hop)
segments.routing: Fan Pier → along the Seaport waterfront → Commonwealth Pier (200 Seaport Blvd). Displacement speed; very short hop — Phase 2 infill.

lines.phase_notes: Premium guaranteed-seat overlay on the proven MBTA F1/F2H market (18 and 19 weekday round trips respectively) — the differentiation is the Seaport leg the MBTA lacks (its South Shore boats terminate downtown; Seaport workers today walk or transfer) plus seat guarantees at shoulder-peak. Explicit partner posture with the MBTA — never displacement. Commonwealth Pier infill stop is Phase 2 (renders dimmed until then).

lines.name: Quincy Line

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone on the downtown approach — displacement speed inside the boundary
segments.routing: Squantum Point / Marina Bay → Dorchester Bay → President Roads (foil-borne where outside the no-wake boundary) → inner harbor main channel → Central Wharf. Verify the exact no-wake boundary crossing point in the geometry pass.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone (adjacent wharves)
segments.routing: Central Wharf → Long Wharf — adjacent downtown wharves; displacement-speed micro-hop.

lines.phase_notes: Year-round weekday service vs the MBTA F7's seasonal schedule — a marina-grade station the public system does not serve year-round, and the network's cleanest 'unserved node' story alongside Salem. Phase 1 runs Marina Bay ↔ Long Wharf direct; the Central Wharf infill stop is Phase 2 (renders dimmed until then). Safe Harbor Marina Bay (686 slips) is co-located for O&M berthing.

lines.name: Lynn Feeder

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan on the downtown approach; foil-borne only across Broad Sound
segments.routing: Blossom Street Pier → out of Lynn Harbor → Broad Sound off Nahant (open water; sea-state exposure) → President Roads → no-wake boundary at Logan's NW corner → Long Wharf.

lines.phase_notes: Joins the network if GE Aerospace or Logan-adjacent employers anchor seat blocks — the landing (Blossom Street Pier) is real today and the MBTA F5 seasonal service (~45 min) proves the run. GE River Works has no passenger dock (see no_landing); do not credit it as walk-tier.

lines.name: Winthrop Feeder

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan — most of this segment runs at displacement speed
segments.routing: Winthrop Landing → around Logan's runway-approach areas via President Roads → no-wake boundary at Logan's NW corner → inner harbor → Fan Pier. The MBTA F6 pattern calls at Logan; Navier does NOT — no Logan stop or marker (held corridor, see held corridor decision).

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Fan Pier → across the inner harbor → Central Wharf. Displacement speed.

lines.phase_notes: Year-round weekday overlay on the seasonal MBTA F6 pattern, minus the Logan call (Boston↔Logan is a held corridor — internal decision_ledger). Winthrop has dense residential and no rapid transit; pure origin node.

lines.name: Inner Harbor Shuttle

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Navy Yard Pier 4 → inner harbor → Long Wharf. 10-min displacement crossing (MBTA F4 pattern).

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Long Wharf → inner harbor → Lewis Mall Wharf. Displacement crossing (MBTA F3 pattern).

lines.phase_notes: Premium infill on crossings the MBTA already proves at scale (F4 Charlestown: ~39 weekday trips on a 10-min crossing; F3 East Boston made permanent 2025). All-no-wake water — this line is sold on guaranteed seats and frequency, never on speed. East Boston promotes only with employer-sponsored seat blocks.

lines.name: Weymouth Feeder

segments.routing: Tern Harbor Marina (Back River) → Back River channel → Hingham Bay → Hewitts Cove. Back River local speed zones not sourced this pass — verify and flag in the geometry pass; fail closed to speed_constrained if zoned.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan on the downtown approach; foil-borne only across Hingham Bay / Nantasket Roads / President Roads
segments.routing: Hewitts Cove → Hingham Bay → Nantasket Roads → President Roads → no-wake boundary at Logan's NW corner → Rowes Wharf (MBTA F1 pattern).

lines.phase_notes: Restores water access lost when the historic Fore River-area commuter boat ended in 2013 (MBTA consolidated Quincy service to Hingham) — a latent-demand signal, not a displacement play. Feeds the Hingham park-and-sail interchange and runs through to Rowes Wharf.

lines.name: Scituate Express

segments.routing: Scituate Harbor → open Massachusetts Bay past Minot Ledge (outside-harbor run; significant sea-state exposure) → Pemberton Point. Sea-state gate applies to the entire outer leg.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan on the downtown approach
segments.routing: Pemberton Point → Nantasket Roads → President Roads → no-wake boundary at Logan's NW corner → Rowes Wharf.

lines.phase_notes: Held at Phase 3 by design: the first Scituate product is a ROAD FEED to the Hingham park-and-sail interchange (1,726-space lot); direct water service launches only if a corridor LOI block demands it. Open-water run — weather-cancellation policy applies (Greenbush commuter rail exists but is slow). Cohasset feeds by road to Hingham (7-ft rocky, tide-constrained harbor — watchlist, not a station).

lines.name: Riverside Shuttle

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire Mystic reach inside the no-wake zone + Alford Street (Route 99) drawbridge transit (documented mechanical-failure closures)
segments.routing: Encore dock → lower Mystic River → Alford Street drawbridge (low-air-draft passage proven daily by the Encore shuttle since 2019) → Charlestown reach → Lovejoy Wharf. Lovejoy is HARBOR-side of the Charles River Dam — never route into the Charles basin or the Gridley Locks. Amelia Earhart Dam is upstream of Encore; do not route above Encore.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Lovejoy Wharf → inner harbor → Long Wharf. Displacement speed.

segments.water_min_label: indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules
segments.constraint: Entire segment inside the inner-harbor no-wake zone
segments.routing: Long Wharf → inner harbor → Fan Pier. Displacement speed.

lines.phase_notes: Coverage/branding line, displacement speed end-to-end — zero hydrofoil advantage by design (entirely no-wake water plus a drawbridge). NO speed or time-advantage claims for this line anywhere in copy. Runs only if Encore/Everett employers sponsor seat blocks. copy.hero_headline: Your dock becomes a station on a connected harbor network.
copy.hero_sub: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network. Boston already proves the harbor commute — the MBTA ferry carried nearly 1.5 million riders last year and now runs a year-round inner-harbor loop. Navier adds a premium employer-sponsored tier on top: 20-seat electric hydrofoils linking Salem, Hingham, Hull, Quincy Marina Bay, downtown, and the Seaport — including year-round marina-grade stations the public system doesn't serve today.
copy.hero_note: Non-binding letter of intent · first service no earlier than end-2027 · premium tier alongside MBTA, not a replacement
copy.hero_cta_network: Find a route to my office
copy.problem_title: The harbor is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: Boston has the 4th-worst traffic congestion in the US (~$1,400 lost per driver per year), and I-93 south of downtown is the 2nd-most-congested road in the country. Meanwhile the harbor commute is already proven: the MBTA ferry is the system's best-performing mode, Hingham and Hull commuters ride 18–19 round trips a day, and when the Sumner Tunnel closed, the state itself pointed the North Shore to the water. Every launch station is a working ferry landing or marina today — no new construction on day one.

problem_chips.label: MBTA ferry riders in 2025 — proof the water works
Inner harbor: displacement speed for every vessel
Employer seats + marina stations MBTA does not serve

copy.precedent: The MBTA and Massport run one of the best public ferry systems in America — we're building alongside it, not against it. Navier adds guaranteed employer seats where the public boats are full or don't go: a Seaport leg for South Shore riders, year-round service at Marina Bay, and a Salem station the network has never had.
copy.stripe_lesson: First employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. Boston already has the best ferry OTP on the T — we add a premium employer tier.
copy.price_anchor: Program band seat-month pricing — not a Boston quote; market-specific pricing TBD
copy.launch_trigger: A line advances when about 60–80 seats are committed on that corridor.
copy.proof_title: Boston already funds the water commute.

Navier adds guaranteed employer seats where the public boats are full or don't go: a Seaport leg for South Shore riders, year-round service at Marina Bay, and a Salem station the network has never had.
copy.proof_worked_body: MBTA ferry ~1.5M riders (2025); F10 year-round inner-harbor loop; Salem Ferry already sells commuter-rate rush-hour tickets.
copy.proof_fixed_body: First employer water commute on SF Bay — premium tier alongside the proven system.
copy.proof_ask_body: Non-binding LOI — seats or line anchor — so we sequence on real demand.
copy.network_lead: Three launch lines — the North Shore Line (Salem · Long Wharf · Seaport/Fan Pier), the South Shore Express (Hingham · Hull · Rowes Wharf · Fan Pier), and the year-round Quincy Line (Marina Bay · Long Wharf) — with Long Wharf as the primary interchange and Fan Pier and Rowes Wharf as transfer points. Phase 2 and 3 stations render as planned, not promised. Inside the inner harbor, every vessel — including ours — observes no-wake speeds. Our hydrofoils earn their time on the open-water legs; every travel time shown is indicative until routes are finalized with harbor authorities. Salem and Beverly legs cross open water, so we publish a weather-cancellation policy up front — and on rough-sea days, commuter rail from Salem and Beverly is the fallback. We'd rather tell you that now than surprise you in November.
